target_customer: Brazilian consumers looking for local venues, and local businesses that wanted visibility (the YC page calls it a marketplace, but 2013 coverage describes a local reviews network)
problem: Brazil's local listings and review market was fragmented. Glio offered user reviews, likes and follows to surface restaurants, shops and drug stores, starting in Rio de Janeiro.
business_model: Consumer reviews and local discovery app, with advertising to local businesses implied; revenue model not stated in sources opened
product_category: Local reviews and discovery (Yelp of Brazil)

founders.name: Roberto Riccio
previous_startups: MaisEV, a Brazilian poker site (per TechCrunch)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch describes him as a former professional poker player.

founders.name: Joao de Paula
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a self-taught engineer and serial entrepreneur; Origin and Mesmer came after Glio.

exit.reason: A podcast summary says founders closed it after a roughly seven year run; no reason given

competitors.name: Foursquare
competitors.what: Global location based discovery and check-in app
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch as a competitor

competitors.name: Kekanto
competitors.what: Brazilian local reviews site focused on restaurants

competitors.name: Apontador
competitors.what: Brazilian local listings and reviews site

technical_complexity.rationale: A review app and website with a social graph for likes and follows. Standard mobile and web engineering, with data seeding as the harder task.

defensibility.rationale: User generated reviews (about 10,000 in Rio by August 2013) could build a content network effect, but reviews were thin and rivals already had listings.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented; Riccio told TechCrunch no dominant incumbent existed.

market_need_then: Riccio argued Brazil's listings market was fragmented with competitors focused on restaurants, leaving other categories open. About 10,000 reviews existed in Rio by August 2013.

branding.domain_note: Company used glio.com (listed on YC page); the domain did not resolve when fetched.
branding.brand_signature: First YC backed company from Latin America (YC page and LatAm List podcast)
branding.community_and_virality: YC blog and TechCrunch positioned it as the Yelp of Brazil; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: A short invented name with notable first from LatAm story, but no sourced identity assets and the name carried no meaning for Portuguese speakers that sources describe.

outcome_analysis: Glio was the first Latin American company in YC, launched in August 2013 as a Yelp style reviews app in Rio with about 10,000 reviews, and took a small reported seed from YC related and angel investors. A podcast summary says the founders eventually closed it after about seven years, but no cause was found in public sources, so the cause is not public and failure factors are left empty.
notes: glio.com did not resolve (DNS error), so the site appears dead. The funding round rests on a single database (CB Insights, $20K, with the Seedtable last funding date 2013-09-01); TechCrunch confirms only YC and YC VC funding with no amount. The shutdown detail comes from a search summary of a LatAm List podcast page, not read in full. The YC page calls Glio an Amazon style marketplace while TechCrunch and CB Insights describe a local reviews service, so the YC description appears to be inaccurate or from a later pivot. The 2022 $12M Riogrande round belongs to a different company.
